title: Dispatch OGF 7: Orchard Is Cut Back While Alderwick Holds Its Breath
summary: A fruit picked at dawn gives the workers a warning they can use.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: The operation beneath Rill Orchard began yesterday before sunrise. Workers exposed a root mass around a piece of clear, unfamiliar wood no longer than a hand. Mrs. Rill identified it as the original cutting Peter had planted. Its glass threads ran outward toward the reservoir channel.

As Inspector Voss placed the braces, a pear fell from an uncut branch and broke. Its scene showed the men withdrawing their tools while a section of the channel roof collapsed. Dr. Saye stopped the work. A second inspection found a cracked support concealed behind the root mass. A new beam was set before digging resumed.

Mrs. Rill held the tree steady while the heartstock was lifted. The fruit on its three grafted branches lost their scenes and became cloudy. At the reservoir, the threads within the wall dulled but left narrow openings. The engineers filled those openings from the channel side. They cannot yet say whether the wall will endure the next rise in water.

The reservoir level remained below the crack overnight. The council has kept the northern quarter closed until the wall is shored and tested. Mrs. Rill returned home without Peter’s pear; it had turned opaque with the others. She asked Dr. Saye to preserve the fruit even if no scene can be recovered.

At 4:12 this afternoon, the market clock struck while North Loom Street stood empty. No water reached the paving. The Institute stresses that the hour in the fruit was evidence to investigate, not an appointment the city was obliged to keep.
